items.title: "하한가 너무해"... 씨엠티엑스 "이익 하락은 일시적 현상"

items.title: 사이클 꺾여도 과거와 다를 '삼전닉스'…"장기계약·HBM이 이익 방어"
items.snippet: 삼성전자와 SK하이닉스의 최근 주가 하락이 메모리 다운사이클에 따른 이익 감소 우려를 과도하게 반영했다는 평가가 나왔다.과거와 달리 장기공급계약(LTA)과 고대역폭메모리(HBM)가 사이클 둔화에도 이익을 뒷받침할 수 있다는 이유에서다.고의영 iM증권 연구원은 4일 두 기업에 대한 보고서에서 삼성전자와 SK하이닉스의 목표주가를 각각 37만원과 230만원으로 제시했다. 2027년 예상 주당순자산(BPS)에 주가순자산비율(PBR) 약 2.3배를 적용한 값이다.올해 6월 고점 대비 10월 저점까지 삼성전자는 43%, SK하이닉스는 57%

items.title: LG유플러스, 3분기 영업익 2천976억…예상치 부합

items.title: SK바이오팜, 뇌전증 치료제 적응증 확대…美 FDA에 추가 허가 신청

items.title: 롯데하이마트, 이사 수요 감소에도 5개 분기만 매출 성장(종합)

items.snippet: 롯데하이마트가 3분기 전년 동기 대비 71% 줄어든 영업이익을 기록했다. 매출은 비슷한 수준을 유지했다.롯데하이마트[071840]는 3분기 연결 기준 잠정 실적으로 매출액 6천545억 원, 영업이익 55억 원을 거뒀다고 4일 공시했다.전년 동기 대비 매출액은 0.3% 늘며 비슷한 수준을 유지했으나, 영업이익은 70.9% 줄었다.당기순이익은 23억 원으로 같은 기간 83.9% 감소했다.이날 오전 9시 30분 기준 롯데하이마트 주가는 전일 대비 0.18% 상승한 5천550원을 기록 중이다.sijung@yna.co.kr<저작권자 (c)

items.title: GS리테일, 3Q 영업익 1천321억…예상치 상회
items.snippet: 올해 3분기 GS리테일[007070]이 시장 예상치를 웃도는 영업이익을 기록했다.GS리테일은 올해 3분기 연결기준 잠정실적을 집계한 결과, 매출액 3조3천143억원, 영업이익 1천321억원을 기록했다고 4일 공시했다.전년 동기 대비 매출액과 영업이익은 각각 3.4%, 18.9% 증가했다.GS리테일 영업이익은 시장 예상치를 웃돌았다.연합인포맥스가 최근 1개월 내 국내 주요 증권사 9곳이 발표한 실적 전망치를 집계한 결과, GS리테일은 올해 3분기 연결기준 매출액 3조3천216억원, 영업이익 1천174억원을 올릴 것으로 전망됐다.yg

items.title: 도우인시스, '글라코어'로 사명 변경 추진
items.snippet: 초박형강화유리(UTG) 업체 도우인시스가 사명을 '글라코어'로 바꾼다.도우인시스는 3일 이사회를 열고 오는 12월 22일 임시주주총회를 개최하기로 결의했다. 주총에서 정관 변경안이 승인되면 내년 1월 1일부터 새 사명을 사용한다.새 사명 글라코어는 유리를 뜻하는 글라스(Glass)와 코어(Core)의 합성어다. 지난 9월부터 사내 공모를 진행해 약 200개 후보를 접수한 뒤 단계적으로 압축했다. 최종 후보를 두고 임원들이 무기명 투표를 해 글라코어를 골랐다. 외부 전문기관을 통해 상표권 중복 여부 등 법적 검토도 마쳤다.도우인시스

items.snippet: 미국이 세계 최대 가상자산 거래소 바이낸스에서 벌어진 8조 원대 해킹 사건의 배후로 북한을 지목한 가운데 김여정 북한 노동당 총무부장이 “정치적 도발”이라며 “황당무계한 낭설”이라고 반박했다. 구체적 대응 조치는 언급하지 않았지만 북-미 대화를 의식하는 듯한 발언도 내놨다. 김 부장은 2일 담화에서 바이낸스 해킹을 거론하며 “미국이 세계 각 곳에서 발생하는 사이버 사기 행위들이 모두 우리의 소행인 듯이 국제 여론을 오도하는 것은 명백히 우리에 대한 엄중한 정치적 도발”이라고 주장했다고 조선중앙통신이 3일 보도했다. 바이낸스 해킹 사건 배후로 북한 정찰정보총국과 연계된 해커 조직 ‘트레이더트레이터(TraderTraitor)’를 지목한 미 연방수사국(FBI) 발표를 전면 부인한 것. 김정은 북한 국무위원장 여동생인 김 부장이 북한 연루가 의심되는...

items.title: 李 “사이버 보안 총괄 ‘차르’ 기구 구성 검토하라”
items.snippet: 이재명 대통령은 3일 보안 취약점을 악용한 해킹 공격에 대응하기 위해 “공공과 민간 영역을 아우르는 범정부 차원의 대책 기구 설치 논의가 필요하다”며 “흩어져 있는 보안 기능을 총괄 조정할 수 있는 강력하고 실효적인 ‘사이버 보안 차르’ 기구 구성을 적극 검토해 주기 바란다”고 밝혔다. 절대 군주를 지칭하는 ‘차르’는 특정 현안에 절대적인 대응 권한을 위임할 때 비유적으로 사용된다. 이 대통령은 이날 청와대에서 주재한 국무회의에서 “인공지능(AI)의 발달로 해킹 기술이 날로 지능화, 고도화, 일상화되면서 기존의 점검과 사후 대응 중심의 보안 체계가 뚜렷한 한계를 드러내고 있다”며 이같이 말했다. 이어 “무엇보다 취약점에 대한 공격 징후를 사전에 탐지, 전파, 대응할 수 있는 시스템을 구축해야겠다”고 했다. 이 대통령은 “얼마 전에는 세계 최대...

items.title: 與 ‘조희대 국조’ 속도조절… 조작기소 특검법은 내일 본회의 처리 추진
items.snippet: 더불어민주당이 조희대 대법원장에 대한 국정조사 추진을 공식화한 지 일주일 만에 당내 반발에 부딪히면서 속도 조절에 들어갔다. 당초 5일 국회 본회의에 국정조사 요구서를 보고할 계획이었지만 의원총회에서 국정조사의 실익과 역풍 가능성을 우려하는 목소리가 잇따르면서 이를 보류한 것. 반면 ‘조작수사·조작기소 진상규명 특검법’(조작기소 특검법)은 만장일치로 당론으로 채택되면서 5일 본회의 처리를 추진하기로 했다.● “국조·탄핵 성과 있나” 민생 전환론에 일단 보류 3일 국회에서 열린 민주당 비공개 의총에서는 예산·민생 정국을 앞두고 조 대법원장 국정조사가 실제 성과로 이어질지 부담이 크다는 신중론이 다수 제기됐다. 5선 중진인 우원식 의원은 “국정조사와 탄핵이 성과를 낼 수 있을지 의문”이라며 “예산안과 민생 현안에 집중해야 한다”는 취지로 말한 것...

items.title: 고개 숙인 김민석 “반명-신천지 비밀연합 증거 없었다”
items.snippet: 더불어민주당 김민석 대표가 8·17 전당대회 과정에서 정청래 전 대표를 겨냥해 제기했던 ‘반명(반이재명)·분열주의·신천지 3자 비밀 연합’ 주장과 관련해 “비밀 연합의 증거는 없었다”며 사과하고 당내 조사 결과도 공개하지 않기로 했다. 하지만 정 전 대표는 “공개 사과하라”고 김 대표를 압박하면서 파장이 이어지고 있다. 김 대표는 3일 국회에서 열린 비공개 의원총회에서 “신천지가 활동하는 과정에서 우리 당 누구도 그런 부분을 주도했다고 생각하지 않는다”며 “본의 아니게 피해 입으신 분들께는 대단히 죄송하다”고 했다. 또 당초 예정됐던 박선원 최고위원의 조사 결과 발표를 취소하는 대신 원하는 의원은 비공개로 결과를 열람할 수 있도록 하겠다고 말한 것으로 전해졌다. 김 대표가 조사 결과를 비공개하기로 한 것은 이를 공개할 경우 수사로 이어져 당에...

items.title: 李 “주요지역 실거래가 놀라울 정도로 떨어져”… 강북은 고공행진
items.snippet: 이재명 대통령이 3일 청와대에서 주재한 국무회의에서 수도권 부동산 시장과 관련해 “주요 지역들의 실제 거래 가격이 계속 떨어지고 있다. 그것도 놀라울 정도로 떨어지고 있다”며 “폭락을 걱정하는 쪽도 생겨나고 있다”고 밝혔다. 최근 서울 강남 3구(강남구, 서초구, 송파구)의 아파트 매매가격이 지속적으로 하락한 데 따른 발언으로 해석된다. 하지만 서울 전체 아파트 매매가격은 10월 넷째 주까지 90주 연속 상승했고, 하락 거래 사례는 강남권 재건축 단지 등 고가 아파트에 집중돼 있어 정확한 시장 진단이 필요하다는 지적이 나온다. ● “서울 아파트 매물 증가” 맞지만 지역별 편차 커이 대통령은 이날 국무회의에서 “예를 든다면 서울 지역의 아파트 매물이 급속도로 늘어나고 있지 않냐”며 “그리고 거래량은 매우 급속도로 줄어들고 있다”고 했다. 실제로...

items.title: 오세훈-한동훈 30분 간격 토론회, 각각 의원 38명-19명 참석
items.snippet: 오세훈 서울시장의 항소심 무죄 판결 이후 보수 야권의 차기 주도권을 둘러싼 경쟁이 시작된 가운데, 오 시장과 무소속 한동훈 의원이 같은 날 토론회를 열어 존재감 부각에 나섰다. 현역 의원 수십 명이 토론회에 몰려들고, 연임 도전 가능성이 거론되는 국민의힘 장동혁 대표도 내년도 예산안 관련 공개 일정을 소화하면서 세 대결이 본격화됐다는 해석도 나왔다.오 시장은 3일 오전 10시 서울 여의도 국회 의원회관에서 서울시와 국민의힘 서울시당이 공동 주최한 ‘세계유산 보존과 도시의 미래, 공존의 길을 찾다’ 토론회에 참석했다. 지난달 23일 여론조사비 대납 의혹 사건 항소심에서 무죄를 선고받은 이후 처음으로 국회를 찾은 것. 토론회에는 장 대표와 정점식 원내대표 등 지도부와 권영세 나경원 박충권 의원 등 현역 의원 38명이 참석했다. 오 시장은 이날도...

items.title: 靑 “전작권 전환, 조건 넘어서는 합의 가능”
items.snippet: 청와대가 3일 전시작전통제권 전환 문제와 관련해 “변화는 불가피한 상태”라며 “조건을 넘어서는 합의가 될 수 있다고 본다”고 밝혔다. 한미 군 당국 간 전작권 전환 조건 충족 여부를 두고 이견이 해소되지 않는 상황에서 조건 달성 전 특정 시점에 전작권 전환에 대한 합의가 이뤄질 수 있다고 시사한 것. 강건작 국가안보실 1차장은 이날 한 방송에서 “(제이비어) 브런슨 (주한미군)사령관은 조건을 따져야 되는 사령관이니 그 부분을 계속 강조해서 말씀하는 것”이라며 “그런데 전작권 전환을 위한 전체적인 평가는 미국과 함께 전략적, 상황적 평가 이런 것을 해 나가면 사실 조건을 넘어서는 어떤 합의가 될 수 있다고 본다”고 말했다. 최근 브런슨 사령관이 북한 위협과 안보 환경 변화로 인한 ‘새로운 기준’을 언급하고 조건 충족 필요성을 강조해 왔다. 강...

items.title: “韓-튀르키예 원전 금융 협력, 방산 공동생산도 확대”
items.snippet: 이재명 대통령은 3일 국빈 방한한 레제프 타이이프 에르도안 튀르키예 대통령과 정상회담을 갖고 원전·방산·인프라 등 전략 분야에서 실질 협력을 더욱 내실화하기로 뜻을 모았다. 이 대통령은 이날 청와대에서 에르도안 대통령과의 정상회담 후 공동 언론발표를 통해 “지난해 11월 체결한 ‘원자력 협력 양해각서(MOU)’를 토대로 부지 평가와 공동 워킹그룹 운영 등 튀르키예 시노프 원전 건설 사업을 위한 협력이 순조롭게 진행되고 있다고 평가한다”며 “이러한 성과에서 한 발 더 나아가 ‘원전 프로젝트 금융 협력 MOU’를 체결해 우리 기업의 튀르키예 신규 원전 사업 참여를 선제적으로 지원하기로 했다”고 말했다. 이어 방산 협력에 대해서도 “‘알타이 전차 사업’의 성과를 바탕으로 새로운 방산 협력 분야를 적극 발굴하기로 했다”며 “공동 생산과 기술 협력을...

items.title: 北, 이틀새 또 ‘폭탄비’… 이번엔 순항미사일에 장착
items.snippet: 북한이 2일 순항미사일에 집속탄두를 장착해 위력평가 시험을 했다. 지난달 31일 전술탄도미사일에 이어 탐지·추적이 힘든 순항미사일에도 집속탄두를 실어 대남 초토화 위협을 가한 것. 한 발의 탄두부에서 수백 개의 자탄이 쏟아져 넓은 면적을 파괴하는 집속탄두는 ‘폭탄비’ ‘악마의 무기’로 불린다.북한 조선중앙통신은 전략순항미사일의 중형 산포전투부(집속탄두) 위력평가와 수직타격 비행특성 시험을 2일 진행했다고 3일 보도했다. 북한은 순항미사일의 탄두부에서 쏟아진 집속탄이 해상에 흩뿌려지고, 한국군의 포병진지·탄약고를 상정한 표적을 수직으로 타격하는 사진을 공개했다. 북한은 “순항미사일에 장착된 중형 산포전투부로 5∼6정보(5∼6ha·축구장 7, 8개 면적에 해당)의 표적구역을 초강력 밀도로 초토화할 수 있다는 것을 확증했다”고 주장했다. 발사 후...

items.title: 충남 방산벤처 79곳… 6년 새 매출 38%↑
items.snippet: 충남도 남부출장소는 충남국방벤처센터 협약기업의 매출과 고용이 협약 이후 6년간 각각 37.9%, 9.6% 늘어난 것으로 분석됐다고 3일 밝혔다. 충남국방벤처센터는 방위산업 진입을 희망하는 도내 중소·벤처기업에 기술·경영을 밀착 지원하기 위해 2019년 9월 논산 건양대에 문을 열었다. 현재 도와 논산시, 국방기술진흥연구소가 함께 운영하고 있다. 2019년부터 지난해까지 센터와 협약한 79개 사의 경영 실적을 분석한 결과 매출액은 협약 당시 총 7703억 원에서 지난해 말 1조625억 원으로 2922억 원(37.9%) 늘어났다. 같은 기간 직원 수는 2412명에서 2643명으로 231명(9.6%) 증가했다. 성장은 일부 기업에 그치지 않았다. 79개 사 가운데 73개 사(92%)의 매출이 늘었다. 협약기업은 국비 연구개발(R&D) 과제 확보에서...

items.title: 한글 점자의 날 100주년… 손끝으로 세상을 읽다
items.snippet: ‘한글 점자의 날’을 하루 앞둔 3일 경기 수원시 팔달구 경기도시각장애인도서관에서 관계자가 점자책을 읽고 있다. 한글 점자의 날은 1926년 11월 4일 송암 박두성 선생이 한글 점자를 만들어 반포한 것을 기념하는 날이다. 올해 100주년을 맞았다.

items.title: 정부기관 이전 잇단 반발… 과천 시민들 “도시 정체성 해쳐” 시위
items.snippet: 3일 서울 종로구 정부서울청사 앞. 경기 과천 시민 250여 명이 ‘과천을 무시하는 이전 계획, 시민은 거부한다’고 쓴 손팻말을 들고 거리 행진을 벌였다. 같은 시각 청사 안에서는 행정안전부가 ‘2차 중앙행정기관 세종 이전 공청회’를 열었다.

items.title: 점점 심해지는 여학생 학폭… 소년원 가는 소녀, 4년새 2배로
items.snippet: 지난 2월 대전에 사는 A(19)양은 폭행 혐의로 소년원 6개월 송치 처분(소년보호처분 9호)을 받았다. 고등학교를 자퇴하고 ‘학교 밖 청소년’이 된 A양은 또래와 몰려다니며 금품 갈취와 폭행을 반복하다가 피해 학생 신고로 경찰에 적발됐다. 서울의 한 고교에 다니던 B(18)양은 지난 5월 중학교 동창에게 소셜미디어 메시지로 돈을 빌려달라고 요구했다가 거절당하자, 그때부터 계속 협박하고 욕설을 보냈다. B양도 결국 소년부 재판에 넘겨져 사회봉사 명령 처분(3호)을 받았다.

items.title: Hoax bomb threats target four European flights as scares spread across the continent
items.snippet: One of Warsaw’s airports was shut and a Ryanair jet landed in Spain under an emergency protocol, the third straight day that threats have disrupted passenger planes in Europe.

items.title: 겨울코트 꺼낼까 말까… “오락가락 날씨, 건조한 땅이 원인”
items.snippet: 올가을 들어 사흘 중 하루(35.5%)꼴로 전날 대비 기온 차가 5도 이상인 ‘널뛰기’ 현상을 보인 것으로 나타났다.

items.title: 중국·홍콩 대학이 ‘톱5’ 싹쓸이… 한국은 올해도 10위 내 못들어
items.snippet: 올해 ‘QS 아시아 대학 평가’에서 ‘톱 5’는 홍콩과 중국 대학이 모두 휩쓸었다. 한국 대학은 6곳이 아시아 상위 20위 안에 들었지만, 2년 연속 10위 안에 포함되지 못했다. 한국 대학의 절반 이상은 작년보다 순위가 떨어졌고, 이 추세는 수도권보다 지방 대학들에서 더 심하게 나타났다.

items.title: Italy-Albania migration deal could be extended beyond 2029, Rama says
items.snippet: The Albanian prime minister said the migration deal with Italy could be extended at Rome’s request, dispelling doubts about the closure of the centres when the current partnership expires.

items.title: US midterms: Michigan Senate candidate El-Sayed becomes Democrats' rising star
items.snippet: In the US midterm elections, Democrat Abdul El-Sayed and Republican Mike Rogers are testing two sharply different strategies to win over voters in one of the nation's premier swing states on Tuesday, November 3, in a closely watched race that could determine control of the Senate. Progressive candidate El-Sayed has so far outpolled his Republican rival and is emerging as one of the Democratic Party's rising stars.

items.title: Bomb threats against European airlines force Warsaw airport closure, affect several flights
items.snippet: Bomb threats targeted at least 10 European airlines on Tuesday, forcing the temporary closure of a Warsaw airport and affecting at least four Ryanair flights. No explosives were found after the planes all took off and landed safely in different European cities.

items.title: [신문은 선생님] [숨어있는 세계사] 2m 거대 활로… 수적 우세 佛귀족 무찌른 英평민 군대
items.snippet: 얼마 전 미 국방부는 인공지능(AI), 드론, 로봇 등 최첨단 무인 전투 체계의 실전 배치를 획기적으로 당기기 위한 국방 혁신 프로젝트를 발표했어요. 이름은 ‘프로젝트 아쟁쿠르’입니다. ‘아쟁쿠르’는 프랑스의 한 마을 이름인데요. ‘프로젝트 아쟁쿠르’는 중세 백년전쟁 중 있었던 ‘아쟁쿠르 전투’에서 따온 것이에요. 당시 영국군은 장궁(거대한 목재 활)이라는 신기술을 활용해 수적으로 우세하고 단단한 갑옷을 입은 프랑스의 정예 기병을 물리쳤어요. 아쟁쿠르 전투처럼 미 국방부는 신기술(드론·AI·로봇)을 통해 기존의 무겁고 비싼 무기체계를 압도하는 21세기 국방 혁신을 꾀하고 있어요. 오늘은 아쟁쿠르 전투에 대해 알아보도록 할게요.

items.title: ​[신문은 선생님] [예쁜 말 바른 말] [469] ‘안되다’와 ‘안 되다’
items.snippet: “공부가 잘 안돼” “그래도 공부를 포기하면 안 돼” 이 두 문장에는 ‘안돼’라는 표현이 쓰였습니다. 그런데 첫 번째 문장에서는 붙여 쓰고, 두 번째 문장에서는 띄어 썼지요. 그 이유는 무엇일까요?

items.title: [신문은 선생님] [알립니다] ‘어린이조선일보 글로벌 미술 대회’ 접수 연장
items.snippet: 어린이조선일보와 에듀조선이 주최하는 ‘2026년 어린이조선일보 글로벌 미술 대회 & 루브르 박물관 전시회’의 접수 기간이 많은 관심과 요청에 힘입어 23일까지로 연장됐습니다. 입상작은 프랑스 루브르 박물관에 전시되는 기회가 주어집니다. 대상과 금상은 무료 전시 혜택이, 은상부터 장려상까지는 유료 전시 기회가 제공됩니다. ▶참가 대상 : 국내외 영유아, 초등부 / 중·고등, 성인부

items.title: [신문은 선생님] [동물 이야기] 나무 잘 타고 물고기 사냥까지… 주택가에서도 사는 ‘전천후 코브라’래요
items.snippet: 얼마 전 아찔한 소식이 들려왔어요. 한 중학생이 자신이 기르는 뱀을 다른 사람에게 팔려고 사육통에서 꺼내다 물리는 바람에 긴급하게 병원으로 실려 가 해독 치료를 받았대요. 이 뱀은 아프리카가 원산지인 숲코브라로 일반인은 허가 없이 거래할 수 없는 종류였어요. 제때 치료받지 않았으면 정말 큰일 날 뻔했죠. 코브라는 아프리카·인도·동남아시아 등 더운 지방을 중심으로 30여 종이 있는데요. 숲코브라는 아프리카에 사는 코브라 중에서 가장 덩치가 커서 다 자란 몸길이는 최장 3m에 육박해요. 이름처럼 원래는 중부 아프리카 지역의 열대 우림에서 살았는데 점차 서식지를 넓혀갔어요.

items.title: ‘그대 그리고 나’ 소리새 김광석 별세
items.snippet: ‘그대 그리고 나’ ‘아직도 못다한 사랑’ 등으로 1980년대 큰 인기를 끈 포크 그룹 소리새의 멤버 김광석(70)이 3일 오전 별세했다. 1981년 트리오 ‘솔개’를 결성해 트로트를 가미한 ‘아직도 못 다한 사랑’, 블루스 포크 록 ‘연극 중에서’ 등 다양한 장르를 선보였다. 1987년 ‘소리새’로 팀명을 바꾼 뒤 노래 ‘그대 그리고 나’가 큰 성공을 거뒀다. 고인의 마지막 음반 활동은 2015년 소리새의 새 멤버 윤기환과 낸 광복 70주년 기념 듀엣 음반 ‘평화의 강’(북녘땅에 보내는 노래)이다. 빈소는 교원예움 인천사랑병원, 발인은 4일 오후 1시. (032)-441-0404.

items.title: 아동문학계 원로 권오삼 시인 별세
items.snippet: 동시 작가로 한국 아동문학계 원로인 권오삼(83) 시인이 지난달 29일 별세했다. 경북 안동에서 태어난 권 시인은 1975년 ‘월간문학’ 신인상과 ‘소년중앙’ 문학상을 받으며 작품 활동을 시작했다. 주요 동시집으로 ‘진짜랑 깨’ ‘도토리나무가 부르는 슬픈 노래’ ‘개도 잔소리한다’ ‘너도나도 엄지척’ 등이 있다. 그의 작품 ‘발’은 초등학교 국어 교과서에 실렸다.

items.title: ‘편견 없는 가족 보도’ 우수 언론… 가정진흥원, 本紙 등 4곳 선정
items.snippet: 성평등가족부 산하 한국건강가정진흥원이 가족 형태에 대한 차별·편견이 담긴 기사를 쓰지 않은 우수 언론사로 조선일보·한겨레신문·머니투데이·헤럴드경제 등 4곳을 선정했다고 3일 밝혔다. 한국건강가정진흥원은 지난해 6월부터 올해 5월까지 1년간 전국 일간지 25곳의 사회·문화면에 실린 기사를 분석했다. 해당 기사들을 ‘결혼·출산·혈연 중심 가족을 당연시하는가’ ‘가족 내 역할을 성별 고정관념에 기반해 표현하는가’ ‘특정 국가나 민족, 인종, 종교를 차별하거나 비하하는가’ 등의 지표를 기준으로 평가했다. 그 결과 조선일보를 비롯한 4개 매체에서는 차별이나 편견이 담긴 사례가 한 건도 나오지 않았다. 진흥원은 18일 성과 보고회를 열고 이 매체들에 공로패를 줄 예정이다.

items.title: Bezier-GP: Bezier-Surface-Based Gaussian Process for Chips-on-Wafer Warpage Modeling
items.abstract: As the semiconductor industry transitions to the post-Moore paradigm, wafer warpage has become a critical quality issue in advanced packaging; particularly for 3D stacking and high-bandwidth memory manufacturing where die-level deformation can affect bonding quality, interconnect reliability, and yield. However, direct high-throughput measurement of individual chip warpage remains difficult in mass-production environments, while existing wafer-level metrology systems routinely provide dense 3D shape data at the wafer scale. This paper proposes a Bezier-surface-based Gaussian Process---known as Bezier-GP---for chips-on-wafer warpage modeling. items.title: Temperature-Independent Logarithmic Current Slope in Interdiffusion-Broadened Silicon pn Junction toward Low-Power Thermometry
items.abstract: With the development of cryogenic technologies such as quantum computing, there is an increasing need for low-power cryogenic thermometers that minimize self-heating. Here, we report an anomalous temperature-independent logarithmic current slope, $d(\ln J)/dV$, in heavily doped silicon p$^{+}$n$^{+}$ junctions with significant dopant interdiffusion and highlight the advantages of our device as a low-power, cryogenic thermometer. Electrical characterizations from 2 to 420 K reveal that, at low forward bias, $d(\ln J)/dV$ remains nearly constant, which yields a voltage-temperature responsivity that is nearly independent of bias current. The observed transport cannot be fully understood with conventional diffusion or direct band-to-band tunneling. Instead, the results suggest the contribution of trap-assisted tunneling. These results establish interdiffusion-broadened silicon p$^{+}$n$^{+}$...

items.abstract: The non-invasive, deterministic manipulation of charge carriers remains a fundamental challenge in solid-state quantum technologies. Here, we demonstrate the concept of dynamic polariton tweezers capable of trapping and transporting electrons across a two-dimensional electron system via the long-range electrostatic potential of dipolar (d-) exciton-polaritons. items.title: Cage-enforced i-wave altermagnetism in boron-carbon clathrates
items.abstract: The spin splitting of an altermagnet arises from a rotation that relates its two magnetic sublattices. In known cases it is fixed by the crystal structure. Here we show that guest-host frameworks separate the two roles. In the boron-carbon clathrates $M$B$_3$C$_3$ the ordered cage removes the translation between the two guest sites and enforces cubic $i$-wave altermagnetism, with six symmetry-enforced nodal planes, for any magnetic guest in the compensated state; strain retunes the class to $d$- or $g$-wave. We demonstrate the platform with GdB$_3$C$_3$: its compensated antiferromagnetic ground state is a narrow-gap semiconductor with spin splitting of 0.19 eV at the conduction-band edge, and its weakly pinned Néel vector switches the helicity-resolved optical response on and off according to the magnetic point group. items.snippet: 국내 건설사 현대엔지니어링은 올 6월 중앙노동위원회로부터 노란봉투법상 하청업체의 ‘진짜 사장’(사용자성)에 해당되는 만큼 하청 노조 요구대로 교섭에 응해야 한다는 통보를 받았다. 현대엔지니어링은 현행 산업안전보건법(산안법)에 따라 산업안전보건관리비를 책정하고 하청업체가 사용 계획을 제출하면 그 비용을 지급·감독하는 내용을 하청업체와의 계약서에 명시해 놓고 있었다. 또 현장 안전 관리 차원에서 안전 수칙을 위반한 하청 노동자를 작업에서 퇴출하는 제도를 운영하고, 일일 안전 회의를 진행해 왔다. 대부분 산안법상 의무를 이행하기 위한 안전 조치였지만, 중노위는 이를 사용자성 판단 근거로 삼았다.

items.snippet: 김황식 전 총리와 독일의 인연은 각별하다. 서른 살이던 1978년 마르부르크 대학교에서 1년간 독일 민법을 배웠고, 총리로 퇴임한 2013년 다시 베를린자유대학으로 건너가 독일의 정치와 법 제도를 공부했다. 그의 40년 공직 생활의 화두는 ‘독일’. “같은 분단 국가였는데 독일과 한반도의 오늘은 왜 다를까?”를 파고든 그는 ‘독일의 힘, 독일의 총리들’이란 책으로 그 해법을 제시하기도 했다.

items.title: Universal model of the growth of III-V tetrahedral semiconductors on polar surfaces: pyramids and glue atoms. VII. Step kinetics
items.abstract: Ab initio calculations were used to simulate the kinetics of attachment of new segments of the crystalline lattice (pyramids) at steps on the nonmetal-terminated surface of tetrahedral semiconductors: GaN, GaP, GaAs and GaSb. These surfaces are wurtzite gallium nitride, i.e. GaN(000-1) surface, zinc blende gallium phosphide, i.e. GaP(-1-1-1) gallium arsenide, GaAs(-1-1-1) and gallium antimonide GaSb(-1-1-1) surfaces. Diffusion species are gallium adatoms at high coverage or gallium adatoms connected with nonmetal atom creating stable pyramids. These pyramids arrive at the steps, and cannot be attached be directly because the Ga adatom at the pyramid base cannot be attached directly. Therefore they are incorporated into the step by additional nonmetal atoms glue atoms arriving from the vapor or detached from other segments of the surface terraces.

items.title: Universal model of the growth of III-V tetrahedral semiconductors on polar surfaces: pyramids and glue atoms. VI. Surface diffusion on a nonmetal-terminated surface
items.abstract: Ab initio calculations were used to simulate surface diffusion of adsorbates on the nonmetal-terminated surface of tetrahedral semiconductors: GaN, GaP, GaAs and GaSb. These surfaces are wurtzite gallium nitride, i.e. GaN(000-1) surface, zinc blende gallium phosphide, i.e. GaP(-1-1-1) gallium arsenide, GaAs (-1-1-1) and gallium antimonide GaSb (-1-1-1) surfaces. The mixed coverage consists of Ga adatoms in the first layer with a nonmetal atom attached above them forming a triangular-based pyramid. The pyramidal structures are stable during surface jumps involving rotations around one of the basal Ga adatoms. Thus, the diffusion proceeds via rotation (pivot) of the pair of the other basal Ga adatoms around an immobile Ga adatom moving them into new, originally empty sites. items.title: Cross-Domain Joint-Embedding Pretraining For Heterogeneous Industrial Time Series
items.abstract: Industrial predictive maintenance and manufacturing tasks frequently contain abundant sensor measurements, but with limited labeled data. We investigate cross-domain self-supervised pretraining using joint-embedding predictive architecture for heterogeneous industrial time series (JEPA-HITS), which learns one encoder from various domains such as battery, semiconductor chemical mechanical planarization (CMP), computer numerical control (CNC) machining, and bearing while preserving dataset-specific temporal scales. We evaluate representation reuse on regression and classification problems under reduced-label downstream training, and leave-one-domain-out (LODO) pretraining. items.title: Gate-tunable superconductor-semiconductor coupling and its impact on zero-energy modes in PbTe-Pb nanowires
items.abstract: Superconductor-semiconductor coupling in hybrid nanowires plays a pivotal role in Majorana devices. Here, we demonstrate this tunable coupling in PbTe-Pb nanowires and its impact on the induced gap and zero-bias peaks (ZBPs). In the strong coupling regime, the device reveals a clean superconducting gap, where robust and non-robust ZBPs are observed in distinct magnetic field ranges. Conversely, increasing the gate voltage drives the system toward the weak coupling regime, where the gap becomes narrow and soft. Consequently, robust ZBPs disappear while non-robust ones persist. Our results establish a direct link between tunable coupling and robust ZBPs, providing guidelines on engineering Majorana zero modes and topological qubits.

items.title: Amplification of valley polarization in an hBN-separated MoSe2-WSe2 heterostructure
items.abstract: Transition metal dichalcogenide heterostructures host long-lived interlayer excitons in the +K and -K valleys that can encode long-lived valley polarization. We investigated the low-temperature valley polarization dynamics in an MoSe2-bilayer hBN-WSe2 heterostructure. The bilayer hBN spacer results in an interlayer exciton lifetime exceeding 2 μs and an anomalous valley polarization amplification effect. Our theoretical model shows that this amplification results from the long exciton lifetime and exciton-exciton interactions. This work sets the stage for long-lived interlayer excitons to be used in nonlinear valleytronic transistors and amplifiers.

items.title: Optical Detection of Coefficient of Thermal Expansion via Frequency Tracking at Cryogenic Temperatures
items.abstract: Accurate characterization of the coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) in nanoscale thin films is critical for predicting residual stress and ensuring the reliability of modern micro-electromechanical systems and advanced semiconductor architectures. The primary limitation is that traditional methods depend on precise thickness measurements or are restricted to crystalline materials. In this work, we present an in-situ, non-destructive optical methodology to determine the CTE of suspended nanofilms by tracking the temperature-dependence of their vibrational frequency. This approach eliminates thickness measurements entirely and works for amorphous films where X-ray diffraction (XRD) fails. items.title: Band Alignment of Grafted versus Directly Bonded Si/Ge Heterostructures
items.abstract: The electronic properties of semiconductor heterostructures are influenced by the local bonding and electrostatic environment at the heterointerface. Here, we investigate how the interface-formation mechanism modifies the band alignment of Si/Ge heterostructures by directly comparing Al2O3-mediated semiconductor grafting with direct bonding. Interface-sensitive X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy combined with Kraut analysis reveals type-I band alignment for both structures, but with different band offsets: the valence-band offset increases from ~0.08 eV for directly bonded Si/Ge to ~0.21 eV for grafted Si/Al2O3/Ge, accompanied by a corresponding reduction in the conduction-band offset. Raman spectroscopy further distinguishes the two interfacial configurations. items.title: Nondestructive 3D Metrology of Through-Glass Via Geometry and Internal Wall Texture Using Holotomography
items.abstract: Through-glass vias (TGVs) are increasingly important for semiconductor packaging, yet their internal geometry and wall texture remain difficult to characterize nondestructively. Here, we use holotomography (HT) to inspect the three-dimensional (3D) geometry and internal wall texture of intact, unfilled TGVs before metallization. HT reconstructs the refractive index (RI) distribution of the glass and via. Maps of RI and spatially filtered RI then localize the internal boundary. Geometric fitting quantifies via dimensions and taper, while spatial filtering separates slowly varying wall form from finer texture. The reconstructed surface supports volumetric visualization, dimensional measurements and spatial characterization of wall texture within one optical inspection workflow. items.title: Trapping photo-carriers in undoped gate-defined quantum dots using an on-chip microwave resonator for charge readout
items.abstract: Scaling up gate-defined quantum dot systems is hindered by the rapid growth in the number of control gates. To tackle this challenge, we propose a different approach where the quantum dots are created from optically generated charges trapped beneath accumulation gates. By shining an above-the-gap laser light onto an undoped GaAs substrate, we demonstrate that it is possible to create and separate electron-hole pairs to form quantum dots. For the charge readout, we use a superconducting coplanar waveguide resonator capacitively coupled to the quantum dots. With these elements, we demonstrate a working many-charge double quantum dot device comprised of only two plunger gates, one tunnel coupling gate and one sensing gate. items.abstract: The coupling between plasmon resonances of metal nanostructures and electronic excitations of molecular/semiconductor systems is important in a number of applications, including surface enhanced spectroscopy, hot-electron catalysis, plasmon-induced resonance energy transfer and the creation of hybrid light-matter states. items.abstract: Understanding complex scientific and engineering systems often requires learners to connect structures, processes, and behaviors across different spatial scales and levels of organization. Although research on spatial cognition, scale, multiple representations, and systems thinking has examined aspects of this challenge, these perspectives do not always provide explicit guidance for designing learning activities that require learners to integrate information across levels. Immersive technologies offer opportunities to explore otherwise inaccessible structures, coordinate representations, and investigate system behavior, but their educational value depends on the reasoning they support. items.title: Reasoning Across Scales: Learning Challenges and Opportunities for Immersive Technologies in Chip Design Education
items.abstract: As demand for semiconductor talent grows, education must prepare learners for the complexity of modern chip design. Instruction typically relies on lectures, textbooks, software exercises, and limited laboratory experiences. Although foundational, these approaches offer limited support for understanding the spatial, multi-scale, and interconnected nature of chip design. Virtual reality (VR) can help learners visualize and interact with complex structures and processes, but its educational opportunities remain underexplored. We examined this gap through chip design curriculum analysis and semi-structured interviews with five participants representing instructional and learner perspectives. We characterized four learning demands: descriptive knowledge, procedural knowledge, relational and design-focused reasoning, and strategic decision-making. items.title: Visualizing Anisotropic Charge Transport in CrSBr using Bias-Dependent Kelvin Probe Force Microscopy
items.abstract: Anisotropic semiconductors offer unique opportunities for next-generation electronics due to their direction-dependent transport. However, conventional electrical measurements provide only spatially averaged characteristics. Here, we employ bias-dependent Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) to directly visualize the response of CrSBr under different electrical bias configurations. Spatially resolved KPFM maps reveal highly distinct, crystallographic-direction-dependent potential profiles. To elucidate this behavior, we employ anisotropic transport simulations that capture the charge transport and electric-field distributions in CrSBr. The close agreement between experiment and simulation provides a unified picture of anisotropic charge transport and bias-induced potential redistribution. items.abstract: Virtual metrology (VM) aims to estimate costly or delayed metrology variables from heterogeneous sensor signals and in-line measurements, and it acts as a critical component of semiconductor manufacturing. While recent data-driven models have improved VM accuracy, most are trained in batch settings and assume stationary data distributions. In practice, however, production environments evolve continuously due to equipment degradation, process adjustments, and maintenance events, making conventional batch-trained VM models difficult to maintain under temporal distribution shifts. items.title: A Mixed-Precision CNN-LSTM Accelerator Featuring Long-Kernel Memory Reuse and Dynamic Quantization for Sleep Staging
items.abstract: This letter presents a mixed-precision CNN-LSTM accelerator for EEG-based sleep staging. To efficiently execute long temporal convolutions, a serpentine dataflow propagates activations between neighboring processing elements, reducing memory accesses by 6.2 times and 2.25 times compared with output- and weight-stationary dataflows, respectively. A hybrid quantization scheme applies runtime dynamic quantization to the LSTM and MLP layers and assigns mixed precision on a layer-by-layer basis, reducing model size by 4.16 times. Combined with a bit-flexible MAC architecture and channel-grouped memory scheduling, the accelerator supports INT2/4/8/16 inference. Fabricated in 65 nm CMOS, the accelerator consumes 0.40 mW and achieves a 258 times speedup over an iso-frequency 32b RISC-V processor. items.abstract: Titanium nitride (TiN) is a promising superconducting material for scalable quantum technologies owing to its tunable kinetic inductance and compatibility with CMOS thin-film processing. However, the superconducting performance of atomic-layer-deposited TiN can be degraded by oxygen incorporation, off-stoichiometry, and crystallographic disorder. In this work, we investigate rapid thermal annealing (RTA) in high-purity nitrogen as a post-deposition strategy to improve polycrystalline TiN films grown by RF-biased plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition. Grazing-incidence X-ray diffraction reveals reduced peak broadening, a smaller lattice parameter, and a stronger (111) preferred orientation with increasing annealing temperature. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy depth profiling shows reduced oxygen-related bonding and a shift toward a Ti--N-dominated chemical environment after annealing....

items.abstract: This paper proposes an open-source automated LC matching network optimization framework that combines schematic-level design optimization with electromagnetic (EM)-aware post-layout refinement. An ML-based surrogate predicts the frequency-dependent complex admittance of individual routes, enabling reuse across matching network topologies and physical layouts for the same technology node without retraining. items.title: Field-resolved observation and quantification of the instantaneous Kerr response in semiconductors
items.abstract: The optical Kerr effect, whereby the refractive index of a material changes with light intensity, underpins nonlinear photonics and emerging mid-infrared technologies. Accurate determination of the nonlinear refractive index is therefore essential, yet conventional intensity-based techniques infer the nonlinear phase shift indirectly from changes in beam propagation or optical spectra. Moreover, methods such as the $z$-scan cannot resolve the temporal evolution of the nonlinear response, making it difficult to distinguish instantaneous Kerr nonlinearities from delayed contributions, including free-carrier effects. Here, we investigate the nonlinear optical response of germanium at $5 μ\mathrm{m}$ using field-resolved degenerate pump-probe spectroscopy. items.abstract: Accurate first-principles descriptions of open, covalently bonded crystal structures remain challenging within conventional Korringa--Kohn--Rostoker (KKR) approaches owing to the spherical approximations commonly employed for the effective crystal potential. Here, we systematically assess the recently developed full-potential KKR (KKR-FP) implementation in the open-source MuST package and demonstrate its applicability to diamond-structured group-IV semiconductors and SiGeSn alloys. Benchmark calculations for diamond-structured Si reveal substantial limitations of the conventional muffin-tin and atomic sphere approximations, whereas KKR-FP accurately reproduces the experimental equilibrium lattice parameter and bulk modulus, yielding 5.433 and 94.9 GPa. items.title: Dipolar Exciton Polarons in a van der Waals Homobilayer
items.abstract: Fermi polarons exemplify how many-body interactions give rise to emergent quasiparticles, providing a fundamental framework for understanding interacting quantum matter. In electron-doped two-dimensional semiconductors, exciton polarons offer optical access to Fermi-polaron physics and electrical tunability, yet achieving stronger and more controllable exciton-electron interactions remains a key challenge. Here, we realize dipolar exciton polarons in an electrically tunable van der Waals homobilayer, where interlayer excitons with spatially separated electrons and holes act as quantum impurities carrying permanent electric dipole moments. These dipolar polarons exhibit substantially enhanced exciton-electron interactions, with binding energies more than four times those of conventional intralayer exciton polarons. We further demonstrate that Fermi-sea layer polarization provides an addit...

items.title: Photonic Crystal Integrated Graphene-Silicon Schottky Diodes for Resonant Infrared Photodetection
items.abstract: Narrowband infrared (IR) photodetection has become a critical technology for the next generation of smart low-power photodetectors. In this work, we present a device based on a graphene-silicon Schottky junction with narrowband response in the short-wave IR (SWIR) regime. Integrating a photonic crystal (PhC) slab in the device enables a wavelength dependant tailoring of graphene absorption. The devices were characterized by photocurrent measurement, which was enhanced more than two orders of magnitude by the PhC integration. The sharp enhancements obtained can also be predicted by numerical simulation. This approach offers a highly scalable, tunable, CMOS-compatible architecture for narrowband IR photodetection, paving the way for next-generation, low-power IR sensors.

items.abstract: We present a comprehensive density functional theory (DFT) investigation of the structural, mechanical, electronic, optical, thermoelectric, and bonding properties of Y2CdX4 (X = S, Se, Te) compounds for potential optoelectronic and energy-conversion applications. Structural optimization reveals a systematic expansion of the equilibrium lattice parameters from S to Te. The calculated bulk moduli decrease from 83 GPa for Y2CdS4 to 68 GPa for Y2CdSe4 and 54 GPa for Y2CdTe4, indicating progressive lattice softening. items.title: Quantifying Blinking Suppression and Probing Its Mechanism in PPD-Treated Single Quantum Dots
items.abstract: Colloidal semiconductor quantum dots (QDs) are highly promising materials for various applications, yet photoluminescence intermittency (blinking) remains a key obstacle to their practical use. While recent advances have enabled partial or complete suppression of this effect, both the degree of suppression and the mechanism by which it occurs are often difficult to establish. In the present work we analyse the blinking suppression of single CdSe/ZnS QDs after treatment with p-phenylenediamine (PPD), recently discovered by Yang et al. We revisit the blinking mechanism in this system and show that it is governed predominantly by the trapping mechanism, rather than by Auger ionization as previously proposed. items.title: FrontierMat: Benchmarking Language Models at the Frontier of Materials R&D
items.abstract: To accelerate materials discovery, language models must be able to address problems at the research frontier. Yet textbook- and examination-derived benchmarks primarily assess established knowledge, leaving performance on frontier research problems largely untested. We introduce FrontierMat, a benchmark of 330 problems drawn from frontier academic and industrial research in fields including aerospace, semiconductors, embodied intelligence and nuclear fusion. Every problem is validated by leading experimentalists and industry experts in its field. Each problem presents a real study and asks the model to infer a withheld outcome or draw a conclusion from selected experimental evidence. Problems are annotated by functional domain, material system and the scale of the governing mechanism; 130 require cross-scale reasoning. items.abstract: Electron-phonon interactions in materials with free carriers are dynamically screened by low-energy electronic excitations, yet first-principles calculations almost always treat this screening in the adiabatic approximation. A fully dynamical treatment of metals and doped semiconductors within time-dependent density functional perturbation theory (TDDFPT) is expensive and numerically delicate. Here, we introduce DFPT+A downfolding ("A" for active space), which starts from the static density functional perturbation theory (DFPT) response of a computationally convenient base system and adds the dynamical screening of a low-energy active space, described by Wannier functions. The required statically screened electron-electron interaction is computed using DFPT directly in the basis of Wannier-function pairs and truncated in a computationally efficient and systematically improvable way. items.abstract: $β$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ photoconductive semiconductor switches (PCSSs) are attractive for high-voltage operation, but above-bandgap triggering requires deep-ultraviolet excitation. Here, we investigate a 650-um-thick, 0.01% Fe-doped $β$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ impurity PCSS with a 5-mm lateral gap under continuous-wave (CW) 808-nm sub-bandgap excitation at biases up to 10 kV ( 20 kV cm^-1). The device exhibited clear sub-bandgap photoconductive switching. As the optical power density increased from 0.64 to 3.18 W cm^-2, the ON-state current increased progressively while the ON-state resistance decreased, consistent with enhanced defect-assisted photocarrier generation. A higher applied bias further strengthened the switching response through enhanced field-assisted carrier transport. items.title: Complete Au-free Metallization Platform for UWBG Al$_{0.65}$Ga$_{0.35}$N channel MOS-HEMTs using Ti/Al/Ti Ohmic Contacts and Refractory TiN/Pt Gates
items.abstract: Au-free ohmic contacts and refractory gate stacks are critical for integrating ultra-wide-bandgap (UWBG) Al-rich AlGaN transistors with Si-CMOS technology. In this work, we demonstrate, to our knowledge, the first complete Au-free metallization platform for Al$_{0.65}$Ga$_{0.35}$N-channel MOS-HEMTs, combining electron-beam-evaporated and sputtered Ti/Al/Ti ohmic contacts with sputtered TiN and Pt gate metals. The Ti/Al/Ti contacts achieved a contact resistance of approximately 7.5--7.7 $Ω\cdot$mm while being fully Au-free. This contact resistance is achieved using a 600 $^\circ$C anneal, substantially below the 850--950 $^\circ$C typically required for Au-capped Ti/Al/X/Au contacts on Al-rich AlGaN, indicating a reduced thermal budget and improved compatibility with silicon-CMOS foundries. items.title: Efficient Simulation of Gate Leakage Currents in Ultra-scaled Transistors from First Principles
items.abstract: To ensure high electrostatic integrity in ultra-scaled field-effect transistors (FETs), thin gate dielectric layers are typically needed, potentially giving rise to (strong) leakage currents. Being able to model this effect is therefore crucial. Here, we show how gate leakage currents can be computed at the ab initio level in WS$_2$-hBN FETs by extending the well-established quantum transmitting boundary method (QTBM). Two main challenges are tackled: (i) the calculation of the open boundary conditions (OBCs) for the gate contacts and (ii) the solution of the resulting sparse linear system of equations A x = b where the matrix A possesses an unstructured sparsity pattern. We demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms the state of the art and can be readily applied to simulate transistors with gate lengths exceeding 25 nm.

items.title: Electronic liquid crystals and superconductivity from doping a moiré Mott insulator
items.abstract: Electronic liquid crystals, such as stripe phases and nematics, are self-organized states of matter with spontaneously broken rotational symmetry. They are expected to emerge in a doped Mott insulator as a compromise between short- and long-range Coulomb interactions, and are believed to be intimately connected to the emergence of high temperature superconductivity either as a competing order or an intertwined order. Moiré semiconductors provide a controllable platform to explore the relationship between stripe phases and superconductivity near a Mott insulator. items.title: PDE-based Bayesian Inverse Problems in All-at-once Framework
items.abstract: We propose a modern all-at-once framework for PDE-based Bayesian inversion by introducing the PDE residual as probabilistic information. In this framework, the PDE residual is treated as a soft constraint with a residual covariance and is directly incorporated into the likelihood function. items.abstract: This paper presents the circuit-level implementation of a mismatch-tolerant high-gain operational transconductance amplifier (OTA) using automatic negative-conductance calibration in 65-nm CMOS. items.title: Characterizing Performance Tradeoffs in Heterogeneous GPU-Wafer-Scale Accelerator Systems
items.abstract: As AI accelerator architectures become increasingly diverse, integrating different architectures into a unified system is emerging as a new heterogeneous computing paradigm. GPUs and WSEs differ substantially in compute, memory, and communication organization, creating both architectural complementarity and additional overheads, yet how to translate this heterogeneity into practical performance gains remains unclear. To address this gap, we propose a hierarchical benchmarking methodology to characterize GPU--WSE heterogeneous execution and the conditions for exploiting complementarity, together with an analytical performance model that identifies when heterogeneity becomes a bottleneck and when it yields system-level performance gains.

This work reports the synthesis, phase transitions, and magnetotransport properties of the narrow-gap Zintl arsenide Eu$_2$CdAs$_2$. The compound undergoes antiferromagnetic ordering at $T_\mathrm{N} = 9$ K and exhibits semiconducting behavior with a low-temperature activation energy of 3.2 meV, achieving a large CMR effect of $-10^4\%$ at 9 T. Below $T_\mathrm{N}$, a distinct butterfly-shaped magnetoresistance hysteresis emerges without any macroscopic ferromagnetic order, revealing a transport anomaly likely dictated by AFM domain dynamics and/or the formation and percolation of localized magnetic polarons. items.title: Numerical schemes for 1D capacitively coupled plasma fluid simulation
items.abstract: Capacitively coupled plasmas (CCP) are widely used in semiconductor manufacturing, where fluid models provide an efficient approach to the simulation of the low-temperature discharge. The model considered in this work couples the electron and the ion continuity equations, the electron energy equation and the Poisson's equation for the electric potential. We investigate the numerical schemes for the simulation of the 1D-CCP. In particular, a semi-implicit Scharfetter-Gummel (SG) scheme is adopted for the Poisson's equation, while the remaining equations are solved using the implicit SG schemes. The proposed strategy can be naturally extended to the 2D cases. Several alternative schemes are also discussed and tested. Numerical experiments compare these methods in terms of the admissible time step $Δt$, total simulation time, accuracy against a reference solution and robustness of the schem...

items.title: Volumetric Nanophotonics for Enhanced Scintillation and Remote Light Outcoupling
items.abstract: Nanophotonic patterning is a promising approach to enhancing light extraction in scintillator materials, with the potential to improve performance in applications such as medical imaging and particle detection. While 2D surface patterns have been successful in improving scintillator performance, the true potential of nanophotonic patterning lies in the bulk, where photons are emitted, transported, and absorbed. Here, we experimentally demonstrate the enhancement and control of scintillation using 2.5D volumetric nanophotonic patterns. Using a direct femtosecond laser writing approach, we nanofabricate square lattices of air holes into the bulk of inorganic scintillators (YAG:Ce and YAG:Yb), achieving nearly subwavelength periods compared to the peak emission wavelength and depths up to hundreds of microns, which fill a large fraction of the full thickness of the bulk. items.abstract: Frontier large language models write correct CUDA kernels for most single-operator benchmark tasks, yet their accuracy collapses on accelerators whose architecture and programming language they have rarely seen. We present a case study of an LLM agent loop built for such accelerators. Our example is the FuriosaAI RNGD NPU, programmed in a recent, sparsely documented Rust DSL, where the loop optimized three Gemma-4-12B decode kernels over 12 days on a shared, scarce device. The loop builds its own target knowledge: it writes and checks a summary of the DSL documentation, measures the chip with microbenchmarks, records compiler-derived legality rules, and revisits this knowledge when the toolchain changes, rechecking rules and measurements where it can. items.abstract: Design-based metrology of academic electron beam lithography (EBL) is bottlenecked by low-throughput imaging. For integrated photonics, where nanometre-scale structural variation can significantly limit device performance, scanning electron microscopy (SEM) is the standard tool for critical dimension (CD) metrology, revealing the structure of devices that is not available from optical measurements. Manual SEM imaging on a wafer-scale is time-intensive, can feature operator-dependent distortions, and yields too few data to reliably close the nanofabrication calibration loop. The following details a methodology that utilises existing hardware in an academic cleanroom: a GDSII-to-SEM software workflow that converts a facility's superseded pattern generator into a CD-SEM for unattended image acquisition and efficient CD and line edge roughness (LER) extraction. items.title: Coherent control and high purity single-photon emission from telecom quantum dots on metamorphic InGaAs
items.abstract: Semiconductor quantum dots emitting in the telecommunication O- and C-bands are promising candidates as single-photon sources for fiber-based quantum communication. In this work, we show how coherent quasi-resonant and phonon-assisted excitation help reveal the intrinsic optical properties of InAs quantum dots embedded in relaxed InGaAs matrices on top of metamorphic InGaAs layers for achieving emission in the telecom bands. By systematically comparing excitation schemes, we separate excitation-induced effects from intrinsic emitter properties. This allows us to observe linewidths as narrow as 21 $μ$eV, the disappearance of slow decay channels, and single-photon purity reaching second-order autocorrelation values in the order of $10^{-2}$. items.abstract: Phonon bursts from ionizing radiation cause correlated errors in superconducting quantum processors. We study prescribed nonequilibrium phonon pulses in a Majorana qubit formed by two $2\,μ\mathrm{m}$ proximitized nanowires. Combining the lattice Lutchyn--Oreg model, microscopic electron--phonon coupling, and parity-resolved many-body dynamics, we track excitation, relaxation, and logical coherence. Without quasiparticle escape, recombination restores the initial Majorana occupations in about 130 ns, while phonons exchanged during excitation and recovery can retain logical-state information, leaving permanent coherence loss. items.title: SLICE-CiM: Selective Layer-wise Inference Control Engine with Confidence-Based Early Exit for SRAM based Digital Compute-in-Memory
items.abstract: Digital SRAM compute-in-memory (CIM) macros enable energy-efficient CNN inference by eliminating off-chip weight transfers; however, peripheral control logic introduces three inefficiencies: bit- slice over-activation at reduced precision (L1), unnecessary accumula- tion depth (L2), and idle precision-transition stalls (L3). items.abstract: Detecting unknown faint moving objects using optical imaging is challenging. Long exposure times are infeasible for such targets, as the resulting image streaking causes a loss of signal-to-noise ratio due to energy dispersal across multiple pixels. To address this, synthetic tracking, a track-before-detect method, replaces long exposures with many short exposures, integrating them in post-processing to recover the moving signal. Enabled by modern CMOS detectors with fast readout and low read noise, this technique synthesizes telescope tracking by searching over a grid of velocities. However, the conventional brute-force implementation imposes a significant computational burden: integrating N_f frames of size (N_x,N_y) requires O(N_x N_y N_f^3) operations. items.title: Back-End-Of-Line Integration of 2-Terminal Ferroelectric Hafnia Synaptic Weights on Commercial CMOS Process
items.abstract: Functionalising the back-end-of-line (BEOL) of CMOS with emerging materials is a key route to neural network accelerators and neuromorphic systems. In this work, we demonstrate for the first time the integration of 2-terminal ferroelectric synaptic weights in the BEOL of as-delivered commercial 180 nm CMOS dies. A novel material stack is proposed, in which a WOx/[HfO2-ZrO2] bilayer is sandwiched between TiN and Mo electrodes. For devices annealed at 450 °C, programming below 1.8 V is achieved with a cycle-to-cycle variation below 3 %. Synaptic weights annealed at 500 °C exhibit more gradual weight updates, while the tested underlying NMOS transistors remain functional after the complete integration process. The trade-off between thermal budget and on-device training performance is illustrated using hardware-aware neural network simulations.

items.title: Machine Learning Hamiltonians with Polarizations for Heterogeneous Systems
items.abstract: Machine learning Hamiltonians use local atomic structures to determine local Hamiltonian matrix elements without carrying out self-consistent calculations. They have been used to study large systems and to carry out high-throughput screening for their electronic and optical properties. The prediction of the Hamiltonian is essentially the prediction of the electron electrostatic potential energy; however, for heterogeneous systems, this potential energy is often determined by faraway features, such as interface or surface dipoles, or even an applied voltage in a nanodevice. Thus, it cannot be determined by local atomic structures alone. items.title: Demonstration of high output power (3.75 W/mm) with 31.8% PAE in Ga-Polar AlGaN/GaN HEMTs on sapphire at 94 GHz
items.abstract: In this work, a recessed-gate Ga-polar AlGaN/GaN high-electron-mobility transistor (HEMT) on sapphire incorporating an AlGaN back-barrier for W-band operation is demonstrated. The device achieves a subthreshold slope of ~130 mV/dec, a peak transconductance of 0.75 S/mm, and an fmax exceeding 240 GHz. Continuous-wave load-pull measurements at 94 GHz show an output power of 3.75 W/mm with a power-added efficiency of 31.8%. This performance significantly exceeds the best previously reported Ga-polar devices on sapphire and approaches that of state-of-the-art Ga-polar devices on SiC, which provides a promising pathway toward high-performance W-band devices.

items.title: Coherent Optical Control of a Single Donor Electron Spin
items.abstract: Coherent spin-photon interfaces are essential for scalable quantum networks, but their realization requires optically bright transitions, long-lived spin coherence, and complete coherent control. Donor-bound electron spins in II-VI semiconductors offer an attractive platform for optically active spin qubits because they combine strong donor-bound exciton transitions in a direct-bandgap material with a potentially nuclear-spin-free environment. However, coherent control of an individual optically active donor spin has remained elusive. Here we demonstrate optical initialization, coherent control, and readout of a single donor-bound electron spin in ZnSe. Using spin-selective donor-bound exciton optical transitions, we initialize the electron spin and directly resolve its spin-relaxation dynamics. items.abstract: Wigner-negative states of light are key resources for quantum advantage in continuous-variable optical quantum computing. items.title: Passive-reflector bounds and robust bilateral nonequilibrium Casimir repulsion
items.abstract: Nonequilibrium electromagnetic fluctuations can generate repulsive Casimir--Lifshitz pressures, but optimizing a cavity at one operating point does not establish that the repulsion survives uncertainty or exceeds ordinary far-field radiation pressure. We formulate a two-sided biased-semiconductor cavity as a constrained max--min problem that maximizes the smaller outward pressure on its two reflectors. In the optically thick-slab limit, identical reflectors admit a symmetric global optimizer, and a passive-reflector bound separates cavity enhancement from the driven far-field plateau. At $300~\mathrm{K}$, a biased-GaAs cavity with $\pm10~\mathrm{nm}$ gap uncertainty and $\pm0.005$ drive uncertainty sustains a worst-case pressure of $2.257~\mathrm{mPa}$ with ideal reflectors. Reoptimization with a causal gold response retains $2.164~\mathrm{mPa}$. The nominal and robust optima lie within...

items.title: Hierarchical Fourier Phase Projection for Local Electronic Observables
items.abstract: We develop hierarchical Fourier phase projection (HPP) to evaluate electronic observables without explicitly constructing occupied eigenstates. Nested Fourier probes progressively cancel nearby cross terms, while exponential or algebraic density-matrix decay suppresses distant contributions. Refinement reuses all previous matrix-function responses to evaluate diverse electronic observables. Electron density and nonlocal forces illustrate diagonal extraction and off-diagonal contraction, respectively. A locality-based decay model fitted to changes across completed levels estimates residual errors from the unresolved pairs without additional matrix-function applications. Tests using fixed Kohn-Sham Hamiltonians for semiconductors, metals, and thermally perturbed silica cover different decay ranges and periodic cell geometries. About 90% of the assessed density and nonlocal force prediction...

items.title: Laser-Induced Rashba Spin-Orbit Torques in Multiferroic Semiconductor (Ge,Mn)Te
items.abstract: The multiferroic semiconductor (Ge,Mn)Te exhibits ferroelectricity, strong Rashba spin-orbit coupling, and carrier-mediated magnetic order, making it a unique platform for exploring the interplay between electronic, structural, and magnetic degrees of freedom. In this study, we investigate the ultrafast magnetization dynamics of Ge0.85Mn0.15Te using time-resolved magneto-optical spectroscopy. By separating magnetic and nonmagnetic contributions in the transient response, we identify two distinct laser-induced magnetic phenomena, both arising from a photoinduced effective spin-orbit torque. Coherent magnetization precession is driven by a laser-induced increase in hole concentration, which modifies the occupation of Rashba split, spin-locked valence band states and shifts the position of the magnetic easy axis. The transient change in magnetic properties, observed as variations in the amp...

items.title: A swept-source dual-comb spectrometer on a chip
items.abstract: Dual-comb spectroscopy (DCS) enables high-speed, high-resolution spectroscopy by down-converting optical spectra to the radio-frequency (RF) domain through the interference of two mutually detuned frequency combs. Accurately resolving narrow molecular absorption features requires closely spaced comb lines generated by large laser cavities with long round-trip times, thereby hindering the miniaturization of high-resolution spectrometers. Here, we circumvent this limitation by demonstrating a swept-source dual-comb spectrometer using two unidirectional racetrack semiconductor lasers integrated on the same chip. The traveling-wave frequency combs are generated by strong RF injection at the laser cavity round-trip frequency of 14.3~GHz---otherwise known as quantum walk combs---and are continuously tuned in frequency by varying the laser drive currents. This enables continuous spectral sampli...

items.title: Inverse-Designed High-Q and Small-Mode-Volume Silicon Nitride Photonic Crystal Cavities for Second- and Third-Harmonic Generation
items.abstract: SiN photonic crystal (PhC) cavities are promising platforms for nonlinear and quantum photonics because of their wide transparency window, CMOS compatibility, and negligible two-photon absorption. However, realizing high-Q/V cavities remains challenging because of the relatively low refractive index of SiN. Here, we employ inverse design to optimize a two-dimensional SiN PhC cavity and experimentally demonstrate a quality factor of approximately 80,000, the highest reported for a near-stoichiometric SiN 2D PhC cavity. Furthermore, both second- and third-harmonic generation are observed from the same cavity, providing experimental evidence of strong optical confinement and large Q/V. Our results establish inverse-designed SiN PhC cavities as a promising platform for nonlinear photonics and future heterogeneous integrated photonic devices.

items.title: DACRI: Decision-Aware Causal Intervention Ranking for Critical Supply Chains
items.abstract: Detecting or attributing a supply-chain disruption is not the same as selecting the intervention that maximizes recoverable net value. We present CriticalSCM-Bench v1, a controlled synthetic benchmark with causal ground truth, paired factual/counterfactual rollouts, and an explicit net-value objective. Relative to a full-information train-selected static benchmark, LambdaMART improves median normalized net value by 5.7--16.2\%, with paired statistical support on the semiconductor and critical-material archetypes but not on digital infrastructure. On digital infrastructure, a domain-informed constant-buffer policy remains stronger, showing that greater model complexity is not uniformly justified. Across partial and delayed settings, LambdaMART retains 33--75\% of full-clamp value. Stress tests further show that intervention fidelity, timing, cost, and held-out disruptions can alter policy...

items.title: Fluctuation electrodynamics of quantum capacitance in electron bilayers
items.abstract: Capacitance provides a thermodynamic probe of interacting electrons. It characterizes the energy cost of transferring charge between conductors, which, in low-dimensional systems, is governed by exchange and correlation effects in addition to electrostatic contributions. We develop a theory of the quantum capacitance of electron double layers, semiconductor quantum wells as well as monolayer and bilayer graphene devices, focusing on the contribution generated by interlayer correlations. Within a functional-integral formulation we show that the separation-dependent part of the ground-state energy is, at the level of ring diagrams, exactly the nonretarded Lifshitz expression for the van der Waals energy of two conducting sheets, with reflection amplitudes built from the layer polarizabilities. The interlayer correction to the inverse capacitance is the second density derivative of this ene...

items.title: THz-Driven Floquet Spin Valve-Modulator
items.abstract: Within the scattering matrix ($S$-matrix) framework adapted to the high-frequency Floquet--Magnus formalism based on the length gauge, we investigate spin-dependent quantum transport in a 1D quantum ring with an asymmetric ($π/2$) configuration of quantum point contacts. We demonstrate the realization of a contactless electromagnetic analog of the Datta--Das spin field-effect transistor with ferromagnetic leads operating at zero static magnetic field. It is shown that an off-resonance terahertz (THz) field enables high-precision switching between spin channels without altering the static parameters of the nanostructure. Driven by an electronic Vernier effect, the quantum interference in the asymmetric geometry yields a selective spin phase rotator alongside an ultra-high-contrast current-suppression regime (``optical shutter''). The proposed architecture is fundamentally robust against m...

items.title: Decoherence of a quantum magneto-oscillator: Effect of field-bath interaction
items.abstract: We investigate the quantum dissipative dynamics of a charged magneto-oscillator(CMO) coupled to a heat bath of harmonic oscillators in the presence of an additional field-bath interaction. The problem is formulated within the framework of the generalized quantum Langevin equation, where the external confining potential modifies the random force correlations and the memory kernel of the environment, and the effective spring constant. Using the corresponding non-Markovian master equation, we examine the influence of the field-bath coupling on the temporal decay of the reduced density matrix of the system. We show that the additional interaction leads to an enhancement of the decoherence rate by altering the dissipative response of the bath. Thus our results shed light on the role of field-bath coupling in the quantum to classical transition of a CMO. The resulting fluctuation-dissipation r...

items.title: Graph-Based Kirchhoff Modeling of Non-Ohmic Electron Transport in Self-Assembled Nanonecklace Networks
items.abstract: Gold nanonecklace networks exhibit non-Ohmic current--voltage I-V characteristics with a sharp conduction threshold, making them promising for sensing and transistor-like devices. However, their conduction has been understood largely empirically, because experiments cannot see how conduction evolves inside the network. To address this, we develop a graph-based Kirchhoff modeling framework that resolves these internal processes, tracking the potential and current of every junction. Although every active element conducts linearly, the model reproduces the non-Ohmic response $I \propto (V-V_T)^ζ$. It also captures the experimentally observed effects of junction properties, network density, and voids, which lends confidence to its predicted internal states. These states show that the non-Ohmic response emerges from voltage-driven percolation. Conduction is governed by how junctions are conne...

items.title: Parity-selected charging and noise-correlated work retention in a coupled Si/SiGe double quantum dot battery: theory and experimentally parameterized modeling
items.abstract: We investigate extractable work storage in a capacitively coupled double quantum dot (DQD) quantum battery (QB) subjected to experimentally motivated detuning charge noise. The battery is modeled as two interacting charge qubits with an Ising-type capacitive coupling and is charged by resonant microwave modulation of the tunnel coupling channel. Detuning fluctuations are introduced as classical stochastic processes generated from a band-limited 1/f noise spectrum. For each noise realization, the evolution remains unitary, whereas decoherence and loss of contrast emerge after ensemble averaging. We analyze the total ergotropy, its population and coherent contributions, the energy basis populations, a passive ordering violation diagnostic, and the Jensen-Shannon coherence of the noise-averaged state. The results show that resonant tunnel coupling driving selects a dominant E0 E3 population...

items.title: High-Fidelity Synthetic Transmission Electron Microscopy Image Generation Using Diffusion Probabilistic Models for Data-Limited Semiconductor Metrology
items.abstract: Advanced semiconductor nodes drastically increased demand for Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM), yet destructive sample preparation, slow imaging and high costs severely limit the availability of diverse datasets needed for downstream machine learning (ML). Synthetic data generation is becoming essential, but current generative models often miss TEM-specific noise, structural detail, and stochastic variability crucial for evaluation. We present a Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Model (DDPM) framework for synthetic TEM image generation under extreme data scarcity. A progressive patch-based training strategy scales from low-resolution patches to full images, enabling from-scratch training with only 15 samples. We integrate a custom TrivialAugment adaptation, cross-process domain transfer, classifier guidance, and RePaint-style inpainting, culminating in full-image generation that pr...

items.title: Controllable Quantum Spin Hall Phases in Bi$_2$Te$_3$-Family van der Waals Heterobilayers
items.abstract: The tunability and control of topological edge/surface states are crucial for the development of new device applications. In this work, by combining first-principles calculations and Wannier-based tight-binding methods, we show the emergence of quantum spin Hall phases in van der Waals heterostructures formed by stacking two trivial quintuple layers from the Bi$_2$Te$_3$ family. We demonstrate the tunability of the edge states under interlayer strain and external electric field effects, suggesting the possibility of switching topological edge states on/off by external control. Additionally, the quantum spin Hall edge channels remain robust against interlayer twist, highlighting their stability against external perturbations. Our results provide a new way to create and manipulate two-dimensional topological phases in systems based on Bi$_2$Te$_3$ family, which can be valuable for practica...

items.title: Dispersive mode coupling in $p$-doped semiconductor nanomechanical resonators
items.abstract: Dispersive coupling between vibrational modes with different frequencies is a major nonlinear dynamical effect. We show that in $p$-doped semiconductors such coupling is strongly enhanced. Moreover, the coupling parameters increase with the order of the nonlinearity. The doping-induced dispersive coupling becomes much stronger than the intrinsic one already for moderately strong doping. Its dependence on the hole density is nonmonotonic, and the temperature dependence becomes nonmonotonic for higher densities. Relevant mesoscopic frequency fluctuations are briefly discussed. The results are applied to Si resonators, where doping is used to compensate the temperature dependence of a clock mode, whereas another low-frequency mode is used as a thermometer to enable temperature stabilization.

items.title: Electrically tunable Crossed Andreev Reflection in Bipolar Magnetic Semiconductors
items.abstract: Crossed Andreev reflection (CAR) is a nonlocal quantum transport phenomenon that arises at the interfaces between a superconductor and two spatially separated metals. In this process, an electron incident from one metal combines with another electron originating from the other metal to form a Cooper pair in the SC. In this work, we theoretically investigate the quantum transport properties of a device comprising a central $s$-wave superconductor sandwiched between two bipolar magnetic semiconductor (BMS) leads. BMS materials possess a unique bandstructure where the conduction and valence bands are fully spin-polarized in opposite directions. By applying independent gate voltages to the two BMS leads, we selectively tune their chemical potentials to configure an antiparallel spin alignment at the Fermi energy.
